comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Installed correct C2Prog version for flashing AEM LDU boards. Flashed firmware 6B33. Compared the symbols files I'm using for backups between 6B28 thru 6B33. They all match exactly. Used Claude to compare EEPROM. Setup a directory with the 3 stock EEPROM files as well as the Ampere provided, the Icon Bronco, and the previous Blazer. Fed Claude prompts and inspected output till something very copy and pastable was produced, checked each setting line by line and then flashed into this LDU. Marked all inverter parts on the sheet N/A where the don't line up because of the different motor type. Inverter checkout now 100%.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Built longer PMU programming harness to avoid PSU balancing act. Disconnected PMU's from vehicle, and upgraded both their firmwares to the latest. Looked up which PMU software revision we were on and flashed those calibrations to each. Hooked up Raptor-Service and key'd on to an immediate CAN1 crash. Will need to investigate vehicle basics like CAN termination tomorrow.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Started diag on CAN1 crashing. Checked CAN termination on all networks. CAN3 and BMS CAN both missing one resistor. Discovered PMU's no longer waking up properly. Pulled open doc for the power block and verified MPR relay connections. Measured GND where 12V should actually be, discussed both issues with Brandon, Billy, and Alex and found the GUI needed to be plugged in and one critical connector to the rear battery box was pinned the wrong gender. Swept and mopped the grease and machine chips scattered around the truck.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Picked backup after connector issue last week. Verified PMUs booting properly now and all CAN networks were terminated correctly. Filled out that section of the checkout sheet. Connected to Raptor-Service and pulled a configuration backup from the VCU. Noticed BMS configuration hadn't made it to the VCU. Tried forcing this from Raptor-Service but was locked out. Checked all faults and there's a bunch including ole BattWakeFault. Measured BMS CAN traffic and found 100% with many error per second. Checked for BMS CAN High / Low swap at all three boxes, didn't see anything but the wiring is extra tight.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Watched the VCU, PMU, and BMS CAN simultaneously while trying to enable the battery system. Looks like the battery wake signal never makes it to the BMS or even the PMU. Checked a few outputs on one PMU to determine PMU1 and PMU2 were flipped. Corrected that and cleared faults. Pumps turned on for a moment, topped off coolant. Keycycled and the pumps stopped, now getting an HVIL fault. Diagnosed that back to the CCS box and HVJB box connectors being swapped. Disassembled that enough to get access to the connector. Re-assembled and cleared faults, VCU seems to be stable now. Troubleshot GUI rebooting every 1/2 second, will need more access to that to continue.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Wrote up finding from yesterdays work. Verified all backups in correct directory and all notes made it to the checkout sheet. Cleaned up cable mess around vehicle.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Downloaded new VCU release and fully read through the change notes. Made a Raptor-Service tab that has all the tags for values that get reset during a firmware flash. Flashed the new VCU firmware release 1.8.4 and checked over the configuration. Adjusted to match checkout sheet. Grabbed logger from pile, verified configuration backup and installed. Verified HVIL now working correctly. Troubleshot pedal out of range fault, still only reading 0-30%. Got the GUI to boot by re-seating a jammed & crooked connector. Unflipped the constant and switched power to the GUI. Cleaned up and checked off punch list items.

comments.author: Devin DuMont

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Troubleshot gear selection issue with Billy. Checked PRND, BrakeSwitch, IMD, HVIL, etc. in Raptor-Service. Nothing wrong could be found, VCU seemed to simply not be running logic. Re-flashed firmware and issue went away.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Built an AEMDash screen to show a similar view to the ECUMaster software, but with some flexibility on view and no control to incorrectly alter the program. Dusted off my collection of PMU CAN integration notes and programs and looked for a good donor candidate to pull the CAN configuration out of. Realized again that ECUMaster Export changes input to outputs and output to inputs. Rebuilt the Output_Status messages with the proper direction for PMU1. Reloaded the other PMU programs so the truck is still driveable.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Continued adding messages into the PMU CAN Interface DBC for PMU2. Manually copied these over into the PMU for a number of the messages. Ran through five or so points in the PMU checkout process, corrected fans that would never turn on. Still need to verify some non critical points like cabin heat and lights and then all the more dangerous points like HV contactors, which I was unwilling to do with Billy physically shaking the vehicle side to side.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Loaded the PMU CAN Interface version of logic matricies so I wouldn't have to re-check all outputs to continue development on that. Re-checked the several channels I had done previously. Ran through the rest of the channels including cabin heat. Marked notes and punch list items that where found. All IO is good except for the AC and heat related ones, as well as the reverse lights and EPAS sensor. Improved my Raptor-Service tab for PMU checkout. Made new logic matrix for the PMU CAN revisions, added in comments and marked changes in red. Removed some spare channels. Verified current trip settings and input voltage hysteresis settings. Corrected the few that were slightly off. Took note of all input voltages as I ran through the whole checkout list and changed their threshold to 1.5/2.5V to increase their error margin. Reviewed vehicle requirements doc and converted that into a VCU configuration. Checked settings in the VCU. Set the battery cell type to a 155Ah cell since there's not a 147Ah one available. Asked Ampere about adding this 6S-2P cell to the firmware. Weighed the vehicle and put the numbers into the GUI. Verified they made it to the VCU. Ran through the punch list marking off items and posted open items to Slack. Ran through checkout sheet marking off previous items as skipped. Vehicle now at 78% progress, has moved from checkout to testing, and has a green card.

comments.author: Devin DuMont

comments.author: Jordan Jones
comments.text:
Comment from yesterday:
"Installed rear shocks.
Attempted to adjust rear ride height.
Issues with vintage v-dubs IRS kit were discovered when attempting to adjust rear ride height.
Welds failing on swing plates adjustment blocks.
Torsion bar side of the adjustable swing plate not properly constrained to the backing plate, causing the plates to walk apart as the suspension moved. When I adjusted the screw this time it actually split the two apart completely. From the marks on the adjuster plate it looks to have been walking for a while.
The old shocks showed evidence of contact with the trailing arm.
Did a bunch of research to determine the best path going forward. As much as I'd just like to buy new spring plates and be done with it, they appear to be custom to this application and though I can find lots of parts that look similar I'm unable to determine compatibility. Every kit maker does this part a little differently. So we're best off fixing what we have.Had @Aharon Adams take a look at everything since he has the most torsion bar experience.
Plan going forward:
Remove spring plates. Straighten the plate and re-weld the adjustment blocks.
Add constraining hardware to ensure the two-part plate can't pull apart. The slot is there, but no matching stud or thread on the companion plate. Looking around it does appear to be something most high-quality kits do.
Add a bushing to the torsion bar cap to press the two plates together. This wasn't included in the kit but Aharon confirmed it's a necessity.
Install a longer adjustment screw to give us a little more height.
Regarding the shock mounting, I believe one of the many parts that were missing from the kit was upper shock mounts which were likely to prevent this contact. Where the shock mounts were intended to go I'm not sure. I moved the spacers around to create maximum clearance, and it appears that currently it will not make contact at full droop. Once we start driving it we can see if we need to address this. On the lift it seems OK."

comments.author: Jordan Jones
comments.text:
@Marc Davis @Alex Noonan

@Billy Arrasmith and @Aharon Adams did a ride-along.

The possible halfshaft noise I was hearing is gone completely. Easy to replicate yesterday, today nothing. The rear suspension has settled about 15mm since yesterday after sitting overnight, sort of points to half-shaft angle as a likely cause.

Billy and Aharon both thought the front end actually feels pretty good on the road, especially with two people up front. Vehicle is ready to drive.

IMO doesn't feel great at highway speeds. Partially alignment, partially the aerodynamics.

Some notes from clickup/this morning.

There are two suspension components which need to be replaced. They have been reinstalled for now, but the new ones are on the way.
Lower arm - shock mount stud damaged from the extensive removal attempt.
Drag link - Seized in place, threads damaged during removal - air hammer slipped and hit between the nut and thread, my fault.
Front camber shim values are out of spec.
The lower torsion leaves have a divot which locates the grub screw, which locates the lower links. These were drilled about 4mm too far outboard either side of where they should be, resulting in an 'off the charts' shim arrangement. Maybe a mistake, maybe purposeful to gain more camber? I maxed out the shim adjustment and my quick camber measurement shows reasonable camber while unloaded.
There was big 'click' when we first pulled it out, didn't come back. Probably something settling, I'm going to retorque the grub screws and adjusters and test drive again to make sure it doesn't reappear.
The driver's side outboard halfshaft needs resealing. Billy knows about it.
The audio interference reappeared a little bit after reinstalling the ferrite filters. Not terrible, but not quite as good as it was. The combination is the same, but the locations have slightly shifted. If it's an issue I can dive back in.
Jordan Jones  [1:46 PM]
@Marc Davis @Alex Noonan
Vehicle is wiped down and ready to drive.

Driving much better than at any point in the past. No clearance issues, even with me and Billy in the front.

There are still a few creaks/squeaks. Some come from the body (front passenger door and rear doors), I think one is from the newly installed rear seat. There is an occasional creak that sound like it's coming from the rear drivetrain/suspension when accelerating. I'm going to leave these for now.

Possible halfshaft noise: I reported it was gone in the AM. After that, I raised the right rear by 10mm to level out the suspension. Noise returned. Lowered the rear end by 10mm again. Noise gone. Does seem to be halfshafts approaching their angle limit. I'm leaving it exactly where it is right now until Ferdman is gone, but there may be some more ride height tweaking in the future. Let's drive and see where it settles. (edited)

Jordan Jones  [1:56 PM]

Brake feel. @Marc Davis you and Ferdman should take a final gander at that. Probably approaching the limit of what manual brakes can do, but there's always power brakes.
Unless I'm mistaken, reverse torque is still insufficient. Don't park anywhere you have to back out of a hill.

comments.author: Jordan Jones
comments.text:
Issues with front beam during assembly:
Upper outer grease fittings interfered with the body. Needed to remove front beam, remove and seal these parts of the beam, then reinstall.
Tie-rods supplied by the front beam company were incorrect (too long). 4" narrowed beam like this one (which we didn't order) need shortened tie rods. Attempted to adjust toe with shortest rods on-site (we ended up with 3 sets), but still too toe-in. Attempted to cut and tap, per the Samba forum, however we did not have the correct tap (M14x1.5)
Contacted Type E Motorsports, who sell shortened tie rods for this application. They could get a set out today, however they did not have the LH threaded lock-nut. Found the correct nut on McMaster. Ordered all with the help of @Ryan Laurel 
Adjusted ride height. Ride height currently set to maximum lift, and the clearance looks good... will see how it settles. Unable to test drive due to lack of tie-rods. Installed a temporary, rough-cut set of tie rod ends (only 1" of thread engagement) to aid in keeping the wheels straight. Wheels are quite deep into the wheel wells now, so aesthetically it's not clear if this is the right move. No rubbing lock to lock.
If rubbing continues over bumps, will need to switch back to non-drop-spindles.

comments.author: Jordan Jones
comments.text:
Here's the suspension update for Ferdman: @Alex Noonan @Marc Davis @Ryan Laurel

Wheel clearance issue appears resolved from my limited test driving on Friday. The random narrowed beam Vintage V-dubs sent us at the beginning of the build fit with minor modification, however the drop was significant combined with the modified drop spindles the car came with (which was only caught when we sent them to be rebuilt). Unless you're building a lowrider you would normally just do one or the other, not both. The suspension height is set to max and it looks good now that the rear has been brought up to maximum height adjustment.

Things to note:
You can get contact between the left front wheel and front-inner-wheel-well when the steering is cranked all the way over on RH turn. The paint was rubbed off before we got this vehicle in the exact same spot. It's only at maximum crank in a turn you can get this. If that's an issue, either a steering stop may be in order, or a mild spacer.
Due the maxed out height adjustment, the front end seems fairly stiff. When we get it driving more we'll be able to decide if this constitutes an issue.
The new beam does not have a provision for the OEM steering damper, which seems pretty common for adjustable beams. Would be easy to add later if we decide the steering needs it. 

There is some juddering from the rear of the vehicle at certain throttle positions. We should verify the inverter settings before diving into this issue. Don't believe this is suspension related but wanted to mention it here. This should be resolved before any significant test driving.

comments.text:
Installed rear shocks.
Attempted to adjust rear ride height.
Issues with vintage v-dubs IRS kit were discovered when attempting to adjust rear ride height.
Welds failing on swing plates adjustment blocks.
Torsion bar side of the adjustable swing plate not properly constrained to the backing plate, causing the plates to walk apart as the suspension moved. When I adjusted the screw this time it actually split the two apart completely. From the marks on the adjuster plate it looks to have been walking for a while.
The old shocks showed evidence of contact with the trailing arm.


Did a bunch of research to determine the best path going forward. As much as I'd just like to buy new spring plates and be done with it, they appear to be custom to this application and though I can find lots of parts that look similar I'm unable to determine compatibility. Every kit maker does this part a little differently. So we're best off fixing what we have.Had @Aharon Adams take a look at everything since he has the most torsion bar experience.

Plan going forward:
Remove spring plates. Straighten the plate and re-weld the adjustment blocks.
Add constraining hardware to ensure the two-part plate can't pull apart. The slot is there, but no matching stud or thread on the companion plate. Looking around it does appear to be something most high-quality kits do.
Add a bushing to the torsion bar cap to press the two plates together. This wasn't included in the kit but Aharon confirmed it's a necessity.
Install a longer adjustment screw to give us a little more height.
Regarding the shock mounting, I believe one of the many parts that were missing from the kit was upper shock mounts which were likely to prevent this contact. Where the shock mounts were intended to go I'm not sure. I moved the spacers around to create maximum clearance, and it appears that currently it will not make contact at full droop. Once we start driving it we can see if we need to address this. On the lift it seems OK.

comments.author: Jordan Jones
comments.text:
@channel
Rear springs plates are back on, everything is good in the rear thus far. Everything seems just fine, the modifications @Aharon Adams made are perfect.

During test drive for clearance issue, noticed front suspension extremely harsh. Traced to the following: when at stock ride height, OEM shock mount making contact with the aftermarket beam.

I've figured out what's happened. This adjustable beam vintage v-dubs sent us is probably for a Bay window bus. If you look closely at the split-window bus photos it shows the bracket tapering straight up from mount hole to mount hole. On the bay window bus it makes an elbow outward, which interferes with the kingpin front suspension travel. The bay-window bus runs a ball-joint front suspension, so it has a different shock mounting point. This did not appear when we had flipped spindles on the vehicle because the shock mount was much lower.

Aside from the obvious, throwing everything from this vintage-vdubs in the dumpster and reinstalling the stock beam, I think we'll be able to get the necessary clearance by modifying the lower shock mount/bushing, clearancing the beam slightly and running a low-profile nyloc with a thinner washers. I will do that tomorrow.

Unable to remove or modify existing mounting studs.. have tried everything. To modify will need to be drilled out and a suitable replacement found, either an exact press-in replacement or helicoil and install a threaded rod.

@Alex Noonan is advocating for leaving the lower mounting point and modifying the beam... that would be getting @Aharon Adams involved and welding on the beam* in situ.
So options are:
Cut, tap and modify lower shock mount / shock. Lower spindle arms need to be removed. Best case scenario we should get ~5mm of clearance from the stock arm to the beam.  4 hours.
Modify the beam itself... cut, modify and re-weld the gusset. @Aharon Adams will chime in with an estimate for that.
There is also the option of reinstalling the stock beam and putting the entire front end back to stock and getting rid of all these variable. This will raise the ride height significantly (see below for a stock height example). 8 hours for swapping the beam.
The knock-on effects of option 3:
Need to get Ferdman's opinion on ride height. He brought us a very low bus, he might like the look.
Depending on where the front actually settles out we might end up with another problem, the adjustable IRS is only so adjustable... it's not impossible that we would move beyond the adjustment window of the rear suspension height.

@Marc Davis @Alex Noonan

@Billy Arrasmith and @Aharon Adams did a ride-along.

The possible halfshaft noise I was hearing is gone completely. Easy to replicate yesterday, today nothing. The rear suspension has settled about 15mm since yesterday after sitting overnight, sort of points to half-shaft angle as a likely cause.

Billy and Aharon both thought the front end actually feels pretty good on the road, especially with two people up front. Vehicle is ready to drive.

IMO doesn't feel great at highway speeds. Partially alignment, partially the aerodynamics.

Some notes from clickup/this morning.

There are two suspension components which need to be replaced. They have been reinstalled for now, but the new ones are on the way.
Lower arm - shock mount stud damaged from the extensive removal attempt.
Drag link - Seized in place, threads damaged during removal - air hammer slipped and hit between the nut and thread, my fault.
Front camber shim values are out of spec.
The lower torsion leaves have a divot which locates the grub screw, which locates the lower links. These were drilled about 4mm too far outboard either side of where they should be, resulting in an 'off the charts' shim arrangement. Maybe a mistake, maybe purposeful to gain more camber? I maxed out the shim adjustment and my quick camber measurement shows reasonable camber while unloaded.
There was big 'click' when we first pulled it out, didn't come back. Probably something settling, I'm going to retorque the grub screws and adjusters and test drive again to make sure it doesn't reappear.
The driver's side outboard halfshaft needs resealing. Billy knows about it.
The audio interference reappeared a little bit after reinstalling the ferrite filters. Not terrible, but not quite as good as it was. The combination is the same, but the locations have slightly shifted. If it's an issue I can dive back in.
Jordan Jones  [1:46 PM]
@Marc Davis @Alex Noonan
Vehicle is wiped down and ready to drive.

Driving much better than at any point in the past. No clearance issues, even with me and Billy in the front.

There are still a few creaks/squeaks. Some come from the body (front passenger door and rear doors), I think one is from the newly installed rear seat. There is an occasional creak that sound like it's coming from the rear drivetrain/suspension when accelerating. I'm going to leave these for now.

Possible halfshaft noise: I reported it was gone in the AM. After that, I raised the right rear by 10mm to level out the suspension. Noise returned. Lowered the rear end by 10mm again. Noise gone. Does seem to be halfshafts approaching their angle limit. I'm leaving it exactly where it is right now until Ferdman is gone, but there may be some more ride height tweaking in the future. Let's drive and see where it settles. (edited)

comments.text: Ferdman Bus Startup: Drew HVAC summary diagram for understanding of which control needs to be configured where. Removed Preheim / Witham blended logic and added in clear logic specific to the bus. Tried various PWM frequencies until I found the least annoying sounding one. Tested fully working, no longer getting heater contactor 2 with no logic changes, dead contactor suspected. Could not hookup to the VCU to fix AC since the firmware was modified and the proper files were not provided by Ampere. Test drove and observed the gear clatter. Found a good stretch where I can repeat that phenomenon. Reviewed the shudder comp manual to better understand the several settings I can change. Went online with the SDU. Made EEPROM backups and flashed my new tune. Test drove again. Repeated several times. Found several worse tunes and one suspected better. Want to start observing torque feedback instead of relying on "feel" before deciding the final tune proposal.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text:
HVAC: Diagnosed the heater contactor down to bad box wiring. Verified AC settings in the VCU and activated power to the slim vintage air unit. Tested AC cold and working.

Shudder Tune: Went back to the default Ampere shutter tune today and immediately got a zero RPM search like before. Put my shutter tune back in and that instantly disappeared, so I left mine in. Happy to go for a test drive with anybody since there's always questioning about is Devin hearing the right thing, but Jordan can also verify this fixed. The gear clack / spline looseness is completely gone, makes sense why I could only make it worse with shudder gain. Last, there was one sub 1 MPH shudder noise I think I can tune out since I can tune it way worse, but I might be getting picky again. If no one else can find that scenario we can leave it as is. It does rattle tthe window but you have to be on the right slope hill with the right pedal position.

Pedal Fullness: Test drove with Jordan monitoring the pedal input and torque. Always saw 100% pedal and 100% torque request, need to see logs to be sure but suspected inverter level problem. Also could be user/cable level problem where they are not fully pressing the pedal. There's a significant difference between slow and fast pedal presses, pressing slowly takes more pressure to reach 100% than stomping the pedal.
